title: task Library
summary: The modern scheduler: task.wait, task.spawn, task.delay, task.defer — frame-aligned, precise, and the official replacement for wait/spawn/delay.

methods.name: task.wait
methods.description: Yields the current thread for at least `seconds` (default: until next frame step). Returns the actual time waited. Frame-aligned, unlike the legacy wait().

methods.name: task.spawn
methods.description: Starts a new thread immediately, resuming in the current frame. Passes extra args to fn.

methods.name: task.delay
methods.signature: task.delay(seconds: number, fn: thread | function, ...) --> thread
methods.description: Schedules fn to resume after at least `seconds`. Precise, frame-aligned replacement for delay().

methods.name: task.defer
methods.description: Resumes fn slightly later — after the current resumption cycle, before the next frame step. Great for decoupling work from events without a time delay.

methods.name: task.cancel
methods.description: Cancels a delayed/deferred thread before it resumes. Keep the returned thread to cancel later.

methods.name: task.synchronize / desynchronize
methods.description: Switch the current thread between parallel-unsafe and parallel-safe phases (advanced, for the Actor parallel API).

details.heading: Why it replaced wait/spawn/delay
details.body: Legacy `wait()` was throttled to ~1/30s and drifted; `spawn()/delay()` ran on the same coarse scheduler and silently swallowed errors. task.* aligns with actual frame boundaries and reports errors to Output.

explanation.whatItIs: The official toolkit for 'do this now, soon, or later' in Roblox. Everything is scheduled against the engine's frames, so timings behave predictably.
explanation.whyItExists: The legacy globals (wait, spawn, delay) were imprecise and error-prone; the task library fixed both and is the documented way forward.
whenToUse: `task.wait(n)` anywhere you need a pause or a paced loop
`task.spawn` to run something concurrently right now
`task.delay(n, fn)` for cooldown callbacks and timed events
`task.defer` to break work out of an event callback without any time delay
whenNotToUse: Don't use legacy `wait()`, `spawn()`, `delay()` — they're deprecated in practice
Don't busy-wait with task.wait(0) in tight loops — use RunService events instead
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
task.spawn(fn)    --> runs NOW (new thread)
task.defer(fn)    --> runs right after the current cycle
task.delay(1, fn) --> runs ~1s later
task.wait(1)      --> pauses THIS thread ~1s
```
All four return/act on *threads* — the engine's scheduled units of work.
tips: `task.wait()` with no args waits exactly one frame step — handy in render loops
Store delay threads to cancel them: `local t = task.delay(5, boom) ... task.cancel(t)`
Errors inside task.spawn/delay/defer print to Output — much easier to debug than old spawn()
commonMistakes: Using `wait()` and wondering why short waits snap to ~0.03s+
Calling `task.delay(1, doThing())` — that CALLS doThing now; pass the function: `task.delay(1, doThing)`
Expecting task.wait to resume at *exactly* n seconds — it resumes at the first frame step after n

examples.title: Cancellable delayed action
examples.code:
local pending = task.delay(3, function()
    print("3 seconds passed — boom!")
end)

-- Player did something that should cancel it:
task.cancel(pending)
print("Defused.")

examples.title: Spawn + defer in practice
examples.code:
part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    -- defer: don't do heavy work inside the event callback itself
    task.defer(function()
        print("Processing touch of", hit.Name)
    end)
end)

task.spawn(function()
    for i = 3, 1, -1 do
        print(i)
        task.wait(1)
    end
    print("GO")
end)
